# Deviation Management SOP Extract (Synthetic Fixture)

This file is a synthetic, hand-written fixture for plan 06.1-07's retrieval
evaluation harness. It is not real regulated content and does not copy any
external standard's text -- see the plan's own threat register (T-06.1-37).

## Deviation Classification

A deviation is any unplanned departure from an approved procedure,
specification, or validated process state. Deviations are classified at
the time of initial report as minor, major, or critical based on the
potential impact to product quality, patient safety, and data integrity. A
critical deviation requires immediate notification to the site quality
head and may trigger a hold on the affected batch or system pending
investigation outcome. Deviation classification DEV-EVAL-142 illustrates a
major classification: an unexpected system alarm during a qualified
process step that did not breach a validated limit but required an
unplanned intervention outside the approved procedure. Reclassification of
a deviation after initial report is permitted only with documented
rationale reviewed by the quality unit, since silently downgrading
severity would undermine the reliability of the classification system.

## Investigation Timelines

Every reported deviation is classified for investigation urgency at the
time it is logged, and the classification sets the clock for how much time
the investigation team has to complete a root cause analysis. A critical
deviation must begin formal investigation within twenty-four hours of
being reported and reach a documented root cause conclusion within
seventy-two hours, extendable only with a written justification approved
by the quality unit. A major deviation carries a five business day window
to begin investigation and a fifteen business day target to reach a
conclusion. Investigation record INV-EVAL-077 shows a critical deviation
that began investigation within four hours of being reported and reached
root cause conclusion within fifty-one hours, well inside the seventy-two
hour target. Any investigation approaching its deadline without a
documented conclusion is escalated automatically to the quality unit for
visibility.

## CAPA Linkage

A deviation investigation that identifies a systemic root cause is linked
to a corrective and preventive action record before the deviation can be
closed. The CAPA record captures the corrective action taken to address
the immediate cause and the preventive action taken to prevent recurrence
across other affected systems or processes. A deviation is not permitted
to close with a root cause of "human error" alone unless the investigation
record also documents why no systemic contributing factor was found. CAPA
record CAPA-EVAL-206 demonstrates the expected linkage: the originating
deviation number, the corrective action, the preventive action, an
assigned owner, and a target completion date, all captured before the
parent deviation was allowed to close. Effectiveness of a closed CAPA is
checked at a defined interval after implementation, and an ineffective
CAPA reopens both the CAPA record and the deviation that spawned it.
